# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination

**RE: Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization — CPT 63030 (Lower Back Disc Surgery/Decompression)**
**Member:** Jordan Foster
**Member ID:** W794852405
**Plan:** Ambetter (WellCare), Commercial/ACA, North Carolina
**Denial Date:** 2026-08-07
**Reference Number:** POC-EE22487639-86426
**Governing Policy:** Clinical Policy: Disc Decompression Procedures (CP.MP.114) — https://www.ambetterhealth.com/content/dam/centene/ambetteril/clinical-policies/CP.MP.114.pdf

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of my requested lower back disc surgery (CPT 63030). My denial notice states that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I am asking the plan to reconsider this decision because my medical records show that I meet the plan's own published criteria under CP.MP.114, and because my surgeon, Dr. Reyes, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary.

Below, I have compared the plan's stated criteria to what is in my records.

**1. Diagnosis of herniated lumbar disc**

The policy states discectomy is medically necessary when there is "Dia gnosis of herniated lumbar disc." My MRI of the lumbar spine, dated 2026-06-28, shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion.

**2. Nerve root compression confirmed by imaging**

The policy requires "Ne rve root compression confirmed by imaging and one of the following:" The same MRI documents "severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root."

**3. Radiculopathy with sensory deficit**

The policy allows for "Radiculopathy with sensory deficit as evidenced by pain, parasthesias or numbness in a nerve root distribution, and member/enrollee has failed to respond to conservative ther apy including all the following:" My records document radicular pain extending into my right calf, along with positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level. This is consistent with the sensory-deficit pathway described in the policy.

**4. Failed conservative therapy — physical therapy or home exercise program**

The policy requires "a) ≥ four wee ks physical therapy or prescribed home exercise program, or documentation of member/enrollee's inability to tolerate." I completed 16 supervised physical therapy visits over 10 weeks, from 2026-05-03 to 2026-07-12, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note. This exceeds the four-week minimum stated in the policy.

**5. Failed conservative therapy — activity modification**

The policy also requires "b) ≥ four weeks activity modification." My functional limitations are documented — I am unable to stand for more than 10 minutes at a time — but I am not certain the records explicitly label this as a period of activity modification. [Please confirm with Dr. Reyes's office whether activity modification of ≥ four weeks was separately documented, and supplement the record if needed.]

**6. Failed conservative therapy — medication trial**

The policy requires "1) Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) or acetaminophen ≥ thre e weeks unless contraindicated or not tolerated." I used NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief, which is well beyond the three-week threshold in the policy.

**7. Failed conservative therapy — injection**

The policy also lists "2) Epidural steroid inj ection;" as a qualifying conservative treatment. I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-09, which gave me approximately three weeks of partial relief. [If the injection administered was specifically an epidural steroid injection, please confirm this in the record, as it directly satisfies this criterion.]

Taken together, my 12 months of progressive, unrelieved lower back pain, my imaging findings, my completed course of physical therapy, my extended NSAID trial, and my steroid injection show that I have pursued the conservative treatment the plan's own policy describes. My surgeon, Dr. Reyes, has documented that surgery is medically necessary based on these findings.

**I am requesting that the plan reverse its denial and approve coverage for CPT 63030.**

I understand my appeal must be received by 2027-02-03. I am submitting this appeal through the appeal address printed on my denial notice, and I understand I can also submit online at ambetterhealth.com (selecting North Carolina and the appeal/grievance form) or by calling the number on my member ID card.

Please let me know if any additional records from Dr. Reyes's office are needed to complete this review.

Sincerely,

[Jordan Foster]
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
Member ID: W794852405

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
